project.name: PathCraft
project.tagline: Self-hosted multimodal routing engine (OSM + GTFS) with a plugin architecture and an embedded web directions app
project.status: working prototype / pre-release; packed global store is synthetic-tested, but full-planet acceptance is blocked by disk capacity and contribution-partition throughput

what_it_does: Parses OpenStreetMap extracts into a mode-aware street graph (walk/car/bike, oneway and access restrictions honored)
Exposes validated engine defaults for mode, speed, and per-highway routing penalties
Parses full GTFS transit feeds and answers timetable-aware multimodal door-to-door journeys with timed walk, transit, and transfer legs via a RAPTOR-style algorithm
Serves a JSON/GeoJSON HTTP API with disabled-by-default exact-origin CORS: /route, /journey, /nearest, /nodes, /graph, /transit/*, /modes, /config
Serves a versioned protobuf/gRPC API for coordinate street routes and multimodal journeys, with standard health checks
Runs street routing in browser-compatible Go WebAssembly through a small JavaScript binding
Ships a single native Go binary with an embedded React SPA: Google-Maps-style directions UI (A/B picking, per-mode ETAs solved in parallel, transit itineraries, debug overlays)
Caches parsed OSM graphs and directed degree-two contraction indexes in source-hashed, versioned, atomically replaced binary files
Builds restartable regional per-tile and global packed worldgraph stores from local OSM PBF snapshots; official-planet publication is not yet proven
Runs concurrent read-only routes against published graph/index state; loading and mutation remain serial

tech_stack.backend: Go 1.25.12, stdlib HTTP, grpc-go/protobuf, zap logging, compile-time plugin registry (algorithms, graph loaders, exporters, cost models, loggers)
tech_stack.algorithms: A* over base or exact directed degree-two contraction chains for street routing, RAPTOR for transit timetables
tech_stack.frontend: React 19, Vite 8, UnoCSS, Leaflet/react-leaflet, TypeScript; embedded via go:embed; optional Go WebAssembly street-routing module
tech_stack.data_formats: OSM XML, streaming OSM PBF, GTFS static (stop_times, trips, stops, routes, shapes, transfers), Protocol Buffers
tech_stack.deployment_model: single self-contained native binary plus optional browser WASM artifact + map tiles from any tile server (OSM default); no external routing APIs, no cloud dependencies

scale_proven.osm_graph: city-scale extract, binary cache ~9.4 MB, loads in seconds
scale_proven.gtfs_feed: official Grande Recife feed: 3,150,132 stop_times rows (180 MB), 87,579 trips, 7,143 stops, 30 MB shapes
scale_proven.gtfs_loading: chunked streaming parser with string interning; ~35 MB zip fetched via make fetch-gtfs
scale_proven.query_latency_observed: street route solve ~20 ms; multimodal journey with real feed returns sub-second; all four modes solved in parallel per request pair
scale_proven.example_real_result: 08:00 departure across Recife -> arrival 08:38, walk 358 m + bus with transfer, real trip IDs
scale_proven.phase_0_4_synthetic_profile: 10,000-node linear A* median: 3.895 ms base vs 118.226 us contracted; contraction build median 21.501 ms and 17.9 MB allocated on one documented laptop
scale_proven.worldgraph_synthetic: regional and restartable packed-global pipelines pass deterministic seam and multi-city synthetic tests, including routing, serving, interruption, and publication recovery
scale_proven.worldgraph_planet: official planet snapshot was validated and processed through node selection, but no packed planet generation was published
scale_proven.profiling: standard Go benchmarks, race detector, and reproducible pprof alloc_space/inuse_space commands; synthetic numbers are not city-wide guarantees

global_worldgraph_acceptance.status: stopped cleanly during partition-contributions; no planet store or manifest was published

snapshot.name: planet-260727.osm.pbf
snapshot.integrity: download completed, official MD5 passed, and PathCraft source validation completed

machine.storage: single 1 TB ext4 HDD mounted at /mnt/storage
machine.ram_assessment: RAM was not the blocker; observed peak RSS was about 2.21 GiB

observed_timings.select_nodes_after_resume: complete at 2h16m28s cumulative, including mandatory source revalidation

partition_contributions.status: incomplete and not checkpointed; resume restarts this stage from zero
partition_contributions.sampled_way_spool_progress: one observed reader offset was 0.13% (49,617,312 of 38,043,122,015 bytes); the 8,424,914,510-byte residue was measured later, so those figures are not one linear-extrapolation sample
partition_contributions.bottleneck: each way-node lookup performs binary searches against the 93.3 GB node index on an HDD

capacity.estimate_quality: the operational projection is low confidence because sample timestamps were not captured consistently; an independent count calculation yields about 687 GiB for two minimum-size records per candidate segment before skipped segments or seam copies, enough to show the current 1 TB drive is insufficient
capacity.recommendation: do not resume on the current drive; use at least 2 TB, preferably 3 TB, unless the partition/storage design is reduced first

planet_compatibility_findings.evidence: official planet blocks contained 224,000-288,000 dense nodes in the sampled first 1,000 blocks
planet_compatibility_findings.fix: raise the bounded block cap to 500,000, stream decoded entities through one ordered worker and bounded batches, and retain compressed entity-bomb plus real-decoder regressions

planet_compatibility_findings.failure: node selection rejected a valid OSM North Pole node
planet_compatibility_findings.evidence: node 269538499 has longitude 0 and latitude 90, valid in OSM but outside Web Mercator
planet_compatibility_findings.fix: accept global source latitude [-90,90], preserve reference integrity with non-routable records, and omit adjacent segments outside Web Mercator

verification.static_analysis: go vet ./... and git diff --check passed
verification.code_state: planet compatibility fixes were reviewed and committed as b16cfdb

resume.stop_result: SIGTERM produced context canceled and exited cleanly
resume.requirements: same verified PBF path, store/work paths, resource flags, and a binary containing commit b16cfdb or later
resume.warning: do not resume on the current 1 TB filesystem without redesigning storage use or moving the snapshot and checkpoint to larger storage

quality_signals.tests: Deterministic Go, gRPC bufconn, WASM/Node, frontend, regional-worldgraph, and packed-global tests cover graph, contraction differential behavior, source-safe caches, concurrent routing, transit, engine, transports, registry, interruption, and publication recovery; latest local planet-fix verification passed 525 Go tests
quality_signals.ci: GitHub Actions runs Go tests, real js/wasm build and Node smoke test, frontend tests, lint, and production build
quality_signals.docs: architecture, Go SDK, JavaScript/WASM, gRPC, plugin-system, roadmap, demo, and reproducible performance/memory guides live in docs/

differentiators: Single-binary, fully self-hosted alternative to Google Directions / Mapbox for orgs that cannot ship rider data to third parties
Plugin registry design: swap routing algorithms, cost models, exporters without forking the core
Handles real Brazilian transit feeds out of the box (proven on Grande Recife), a market underserved by polished routing tooling
Whole stack is inspectable: graph debug overlays (street classes, intersections, stops) built into the shipped UI
current_gaps_be_honest: No geocoding/search-by-name (coordinates and map clicks only)
GTFS calendar/service-day filtering not applied (all trips treated as running); no GTFS-realtime
No turn-by-turn instructions, no traffic, bike/car use heuristic speeds
City routing remains the only real-data serving scale proven; no full contraction hierarchies, horizontal scaling story, auth, rate limiting, or multi-tenant features
gRPC is plaintext and unauthenticated; loopback default is prototype-safe, not public-internet hardening
WASM supports synchronous street routing only; no GTFS, workers, streaming input, or npm release
Base street graph remains resident beside contraction index; concurrent hot reload and graph mutation are unsupported
Router marked by author as debug/demo grade rather than production
Packed global format is synthetic-tested, but the official planet build has not reached publication
Current contribution partition performs billions of random disk-index lookups and is impractically slow on an HDD
Current planet work/store layout is projected to need roughly 1.2-1.6 TiB peak; the tested 1 TB filesystem is insufficient
No long-distance routing hierarchy exists; global chunks still support bounded local/regional routes only
No packaged releases, Docker image, or hosted demo yet
near_term_roadmap_hints: Redesign global contribution partitioning to avoid per-reference binary searches and the projected ~672 GiB duplicated contribution spool
Add a representative extract capacity benchmark that reports peak RSS, work bytes, store bytes, throughput, and a preflight disk requirement before planet builds
Resume official-planet acceptance only on at least 2 TB storage, preferably 3 TB, or after reducing peak storage below the current 1 TB filesystem
Docker packaging, tagged releases, generated SDK packaging, and hosted demo
Geocoder integration (e.g., Nominatim/Photon) for address search
More city feeds to prove generality (catalog of Brazilian capitals)
Profile representative city extracts and set latency/memory budgets before considering profile-specific contraction hierarchies
possible_business_surfaces_raw_facts_for: Transit agencies / city governments in Brazil publish GTFS but lack rider-facing journey planners they control
Logistics and delivery companies need self-hosted routing where per-request API pricing (Google: ~USD 5-10 per 1000 directions calls) dominates costs
Urban-planning consultancies need multimodal accessibility analysis on open data
White-label embedded directions widget for real-estate/tourism portals
The plugin architecture allows selling proprietary cost models (safety, accessibility, low-emission routing) on an open core
